blocks.content: The Pacific Ring of Fire accounts for nearly 68% of the total earthquakes on Earth due to intense convergent plate boundary interactions.

items: Deep-focus earthquakes occur almost exclusively along subduction zones in convergent plate boundaries like the Circum-Pacific Belt.
India is divided into four seismic risk zones by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS): Zone II (Low), Zone III (Moderate), Zone IV (High), and Zone V (Very High). Zone I is no longer used.
Questions frequently contrast shallow-focus earthquakes at divergent ridges with deep-focus earthquakes along ocean trenches.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Circum-Pacific Belt, known as the Pacific Ring of Fire, accounts for roughly 68% of global earthquake activity along convergent margins.
The Mid-Continental Belt stretches from the Alpine region across the Himalayas to Indonesia, encompassing around 21% of worldwide earthquakes.
Earthquakes are categorized by focal depth into shallow-focus (<70 km), intermediate-focus (70–300 km), and deep-focus (>300 km).
Mid-oceanic ridges witness frequent shallow-focus earthquakes created by divergent tectonic movements and seafloor spreading.
India's active seismic region falls under the Alpine-Himalayan Belt and is classified into four distinct seismic threat zones (Zone II to Zone V).
